prompt_text: My roof has hail damage in Denver. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you a short, practical plan and the exact kinds of roofing companies to call — plus why each is important — and the questions to ask when you call. If you want, I can then look up specific company names near your address or ZIP code (I’ll need your ZIP or neighborhood).

Immediate priorities
- Document damage with photos/videos and date/time.
- Call your insurance company to report the claim (most insurers require prompt notice).
- Get temporary tarping if you have active leaks (don’t wait for the full estimate).

Who to call (call at least 3 different providers)
1) A local GAF/CertainTeed/IKO “Master” or certified contractor
- Why: These contractors are vetted by major shingle manufacturers, have training about proper installation, and can offer manufacturer-backed warranties. They tend to use certified materials and stand behind workmanship.

2) A local storm-restoration specialist who works regularly with insurance claims
- Why: Storm specialists know how to document hail damage to match insurance adjusters’ expectations, prepare Xactimate-style estimates, and handle claims efficiently. They often help with temporary tarping and emergency repairs.

3) Your insurer’s preferred vendor (with caution)
- Why: Quick appointment and claims coordination. Caveat: some preferred vendors push specific repairs or sign-over-of-claim forms; still get at least one independent estimate to compare.

4) A trusted local independent roofer with strong long-term reviews and references
- Why: Long-standing local companies can offer personal accountability, faster scheduling, and references from your neighborhood.

5) (Optional) A public adjuster — only if the claim seems underpaid or complex
- Why: They negotiate with the insurance company on your behalf for a fee, which can be worth it for large or disputed claims.

How to find specific companies now
- Use manufacturer locators: GAF Master Elite locator or CertainTeed Select ShingleMasters. These show certified local contractors.
- Check Colorado Roofing Association and National Roofing Contractors Association (NRCA) member lists for Colorado/Denver.
- Use Google Business + Yelp + BBB to compare reviews and years in business.
- Ask neighbors (Denver neighborhoods often share lists after storms).

What to ask every roofer on the phone
- Are you licensed in Colorado and insured (liability + worker’s comp)? Can you email a certificate?
- How many years in business in the Denver area? Any local references I can call?
- Do you have experience handling hail claims and working with insurance adjusters?
- Do you provide a written estimate with line-item materials and labor? Do you use Xactimate?
- What manufacturer certifications do you hold (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed, Owens Corning)?
- Do you offer workmanship warranties and manufacturer warranties? Are they transferable?
- Will you handle permits and final inspections?
- What is your payment schedule? Do you require an AOB (assignment of benefits)?
- Do you provide a written lien waiver on final payment?
- Can you do temporary tarping/board-up immediately if needed?

Red flags to avoid
- Door-to-door storm “chaser” contractors pressuring you to sign today.
- High-pressure “sign now” tactics, requiring full payment up front, or asking you to sign over your insurance check (AOB) without full explanation.
- Vague written estimates or “we’ll figure it out” contracts.
- Contractors who insist you repair everything immediately without letting your insurer inspect first (if there’s time).

How to compare the estimates
- Make sure each estimate lists the same scope, materials (brand/type/color), removal of old shingles vs overlay, underlayment, flashing, vents, rake and drip edge, ice & water shield, disposal fees, permits.
- Prefer detailed line-item pricing and written material warranties.
- Confirm who will handle any roof decking replacement if rot is found and how that’s charged.

If you want, I can:
- Look up 4–6 specific, well-reviewed roofing contractors that serve your Denver ZIP code and list pros/cons for each — give me your ZIP or neighborhood.
- Or walk you through a script to use on calls and a comparison sheet template.

Which option would you prefer?
